shared_elements: human figure in low relief, shown in profile/frontal-limbed convention
carved relief on a flat panel-like surface
justification: Both surfaces carry low-relief carving in which a human-like figure with defined limbs and head can be read, which is about as generic a correspondence as two carving traditions can share. A depicts a fully articulated composition — a framed lunette with a winged disc above, a large standing figure before an offering table with smaller attendant figures, and dense rows of inscribed text filling the field below — whereas B shows a single, sprawling, loosely outlined figure with no framing, no accompanying disc, no offering furniture and no script.
